findings.quote: Raising both sides of the adiabatic relation to the power one over (γ−1) turns the volume ratio into a cube root here.
findings.note: The direct statement is that the temperature ratio equals the VOLUME ratio raised to the power (γ−1) = 1/3, that is, the cube root of 8. As written, the sentence names the exponent 1/(γ−1) = 3, which a student can read as instructing them to cube the volume ratio, giving 8 cubed instead of the cube root of 8. The sentence is defensible on a longer route (cubing TV^(1/3) = C gives T³V = C³, and solving for T then puts the volume ratio under a cube root), so it is not false, but it states the exponent that is not the one applied to the volume ratio in the equation beside it.
findings.fix: Since gamma minus one is one third, the temperature ratio is the volume ratio raised to the power one third, that is the cube root of 8, which is 2.

notes: My own solve: the isothermal expansion leaves the gas at T0 and 8V0. Adiabatic compression back to V0 obeys TV^(gamma-1) = constant with gamma - 1 = 1/3, so T_final = T0 x 8^(1/3) = 2 T0. Average kinetic energy per molecule is (3/2)kT, proportional to T, so the ratio is 2.0, option 3. Verified in python: 8^(1/3) = 2.000 and (1/8)^(1/3) = 0.500, so common_mistakes[0] is a genuine route and its stated outcome (a fall to half the original temperature) is exactly right. The initial pressure P0 is not needed. difficulty "hard" is fair for a two-process chain.
